title: Vacuum-induced interference in light scattering by multilevel atomic chains
authors: Aleksei Konovalov, Giovanna Morigi, Nicola Piovella
abstract: We investigate cooperative light scattering by an ordered chain of multilevel atoms, which possess two quasi-resonant transitions with parallel dipole moments. Interference between dipole transitions induced by coupling with the vacuum gives rise to so called cross-damping and cross-shifts, that modify the incoherent and coherent dynamics and can be manifest in the spectroscopic properties of the emitted light. We determine the excitation spectrum when the atomic chain is driven by an external laser in the limit in which the dipolar transitions can be described by harmonic oscillators and the scattering is coherent. We show that the interplay of multilevel interference and superradiance can give rise to measurable effects in chains of alkali-metal atoms.
summary: This paper theoretically analyzes how vacuum fluctuations induce interference effects—cross-damping and cross-shifts—when light scatters from an ordered chain of multilevel atoms. By modeling the system using coupled dipole equations, the authors predict that these collective interference terms manifest as measurable shifts and changes in linewidths within the excitation spectrum. The findings are significant for understanding quantum light-matter interactions in structured atomic media.
main_problem: The study investigates vacuum-induced interference effects, specifically cross-damping and cross-shifts, that modify light scattering dynamics in ordered chains of multilevel atoms.
main_result: The interplay between multilevel interference and superradiance can lead to measurable spectral modifications (linewidths and shifts) in alkali-metal atomic chains when spatial periodicity is considered.
method: The authors use the Model of Coupled Coherent Dipoles (MCD), solving equations derived from a master equation, and employing perturbation theory for the excitation spectrum analysis.
model_or_system: The system is an ordered 1D array of multilevel quantum emitters, each with two quasi-resonant transitions. The dynamics are governed by coupled coherence equations incorporating interatomic coupling via Green's functions.
key_observables: Photon-count signal (excitation spectrum) $S_{\Omega}(\delta L)$, linewidth ($	ext{CDR}$), and line shift ($	ext{CLS}$).
important_parameters: Weak saturation regime ($N\Omega_i \ll |\dots|$); chain periodicity ($a$); energy gap ($\delta\omega$).

figures_summary: Figures compare numerical photon-count signals for Na and Li atoms against mean-field theory at different orders of perturbation ($\epsilon$). Other figures show the dependence of $	ext{CLS}$ and $	ext{CDR}$ on chain period $a$, highlighting cross-interference contributions.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the MCD, provides an analytical solution for a general three-level system, analyzes excitation spectra numerically, and finally examines the robustness against atomic vibrations.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses open quantum systems dynamics in structured media, providing quantitative predictions for collective effects (superradiance, cross-damping) that are sensitive to spatial arrangement, which is a key area in quantum optics.

In this work we assess the magnitude of this interference on coherent scattering when the emitters form a chain.
